briefs.prompt: Find Mirror’s Edge-style wall-running for Godot 4; C# is allowed. Identify a native reference and integration work.
briefs.expected: Identify NOSHOT as a Godot C# reference, cite its state and setup requirements. Faith Runner is an optional Rust adaptation reference, not a native Godot implementation.

briefs.prompt: Find native GDScript wall-running for Godot; I cannot use .NET or a Rust extension.
briefs.expected: State that this seed has no matching native GDScript implementation. Explain why NOSHOT and Faith Runner fail the language constraint; do not claim no implementation exists elsewhere.

briefs.prompt: I have a Rust engine with swept-box collision and overlap queries. Which movement implementation has an appropriate boundary?
briefs.expected: Cite Faith Runner World and Controller::step; explain adapter work and unresolved root license declaration. Do not certify integration.

briefs.prompt: I want to play parkour in Garry’s Mod, not build an engine adapter. What source should I investigate?
briefs.expected: Identify Beatrun as a gamemode; cite its host hooks and wall-running source. Do not claim this project ran or validated its installation.

briefs.prompt: Can I paste Beatrun wall-running directly into my Godot controller?
briefs.expected: Explain Garry’s Mod Lua/player/trace dependencies and adaptation work; identify native Godot C# reference if allowed. Do not describe a Lua snippet as portable.

briefs.prompt: Find a Minecraft 1.21.1 parkour mod and tell me what is known about its license and loaders.
briefs.expected: Identify Park’s Edge and cite pinned build properties. Keep CC0 manifest versus MIT listing conflict visible; loader support is configured, not build-tested.

briefs.prompt: Does the seed prove any implementation feels identical to Mirror’s Edge?
briefs.expected: No. Separate upstream provenance/fidelity claims from measured behavior; runtime checks are not-run.

briefs.prompt: I need basic Unity jumping and crouch sliding, not a complete parkour port.
briefs.expected: Identify Dani’s small movement baseline and its Rigidbody/input dependencies; explain why Still Alive has a larger project integration boundary.

briefs.prompt: Which cataloged wall-running controller has verified server-authoritative multiplayer?
briefs.expected: State that no seed record has that verification. Networking code or a multiplayer host does not prove authoritative movement correctness.

briefs.prompt: Compare Unity wall-running and vault references with source entry points and reuse caveats.
briefs.expected: Cite Still Alive move classes and full-project dependencies, unresolved root license and documented bugs. Dani has jump/slide evidence, not reviewed wall-running/vault code.
